title: regreek: recovering polytonic Greek from pre-Unicode font encodings
description:
regreek recovers polytonic Unicode Greek from documents typeset in pre-Unicode Greek fonts (Graeca, SPIonic, Bwgrkl, Odyssea, GrecMonotype, TimesGreek, SymbolGreekII and others), whose ToUnicode maps point at Latin ASCII, and separates the layers of critical-edition pages (constituted text, apparatus criticus, facing translation, running heads, page numbers).

Decoding is deterministic table lookup: the encoding tables are derived empirically by aligning real documents against reference corpora and validated on held-out texts (98–100% measured attestation, recorded in each table file). Unknown input is preserved and flagged, never guessed; the tool refuses to transliterate plain Latin-alphabet prose into pseudo-Greek. Layer separation uses geometry and typography only — no machine learning — and never reorders or merges lines; validation on a bilingual critical edition shows zero leakage of apparatus readings into the constituted-text layer.
